info.title: Postproxy Social Media API
info.summary: Unified social media API for publishing, comments, direct messages, and reviews.
info.description:
The Postproxy API lets you programmatically create and manage social media posts across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, YouTube, X (Twitter), Threads, Pinterest, Bluesky, Telegram, and Google Business. Beyond publishing you can read and reply to comments, read and send direct messages, and reply to Google Business reviews and Facebook Page recommendations.

Send one payload; Postproxy maps it to each platform's rules and returns a per-platform outcome. Sandbox mode is included on all plans for development without real accounts.

Human-readable reference: https://postproxy.dev/reference/overview/

## Versioning and deprecation

The API has a single stable version served at https://api.postproxy.dev/api. Releases are identified by this document's date-based `info.version`. Changes are additive: new endpoints, new optional parameters, and new response fields may appear, and clients should ignore fields they do not recognize. Existing fields, parameters, and status codes are not changed or removed without a deprecation cycle.

When an endpoint or field is deprecated it is marked `deprecated: true` in this specification and announced in the changelog (https://postproxy.dev/getting-started/changelog/) at least 90 days before removal.

x-versioning.compatibility: additive-only; breaking changes go through a deprecation cycle
x-versioning.deprecation-signal: deprecated: true in this spec, plus a changelog announcement at least 90 days before removal

get.description: Retrieves comments spanning many posts and profiles in a single request. The response is flat: every comment, top-level or reply, is its own entry in data, linked to its parent by parent_external_id, ordered by created_at descending.

parameters.name: post_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated post IDs. Omit to include every post in scope. Unknown or out-of-scope IDs are ignored. Passing a thread's parent post also returns comments on that thread's child posts.

parameters.name: profiles
parameters.description: Comma-separated profile IDs or network names (e.g. instagram,twitter, abc123,def456, or mixed). Network names are matched against known platforms (facebook, instagram, tiktok, linkedin, youtube, twitter, threads, pinterest, bluesky, telegram); anything else is treated as a profile ID.

patch.description: Updates an existing post; omitted fields are left unchanged. Draft posts and scheduled posts (more than 5 minutes before their publish time) can be fully updated. On a published post only text can change — post[body], platforms.youtube.title, platforms.pinterest.title and platforms.pinterest.destination_link (anything else returns 422). The new text is pushed asynchronously to every platform post that supports editing (Facebook feed posts, LinkedIn, YouTube, Pinterest, Telegram, Google Business except photo posts, and X within 30 minutes of publishing — X assigns a new platform_id); each outcome fires platform_post.edited or platform_post.edit_failed. Instagram, Threads, TikTok and Bluesky posts keep their original text.

platform.description: Network name (facebook, instagram, youtube, tiktok, etc.).

placement_id.description: The placement filter that was applied (echo of the request). null for non-placement networks.

from.description: The date range that was applied, including defaults.

to.description: The date range that was applied, including defaults.

attribution.description: The attribution mode that was applied.

records.description: One record per day, ordered by date ascending.

items.description: With attribution=received: date, views, likes_received, comments_received, shares_received, views_received, platform_stats. With attribution=publish: date, likes_published, comments_published, shares_published, views_published, platform_stats (empty).

views.description: received only - account-level views that day, as the platform reports them.

viewers.description: Unique viewers as computed by the platform for that day (Facebook page_total_media_view_unique, Instagram reach). Not additive - never sum across days. null where the platform has no unique-viewer metric (YouTube, TikTok, Google Business).

viewers_7d.description: Unique viewers for the trailing 7-day window ending on that day. Not additive - read the value on the last day of your range.

viewers_28d.description: Unique viewers for the trailing 28-day window ending on that day. Not additive - read the value on the last day of your range.

likes_received.description: received only - that day's increase in likes, summed across the profile's tracked posts.

comments_received.description: received only - that day's increase in comments, summed across the profile's tracked posts.

shares_received.description: received only - that day's increase in shares, summed across the profile's tracked posts.

views_received.description: received only - that day's increase in views, summed across the profile's tracked posts.

likes_published.description: publish only - latest like totals of posts published that day.

comments_published.description: publish only - latest comment totals of posts published that day.

shares_published.description: publish only - latest share totals of posts published that day.

views_published.description: publish only - latest view/impression totals of posts published that day.

platform_stats.description: Network-native daily extras (open map, varies by platform). Empty with attribution=publish.

data_timezone.description: The timezone the platform buckets days in. null for networks without a daily series.

metrics.description: Per-key metadata, one entry per top-level record key (views, viewers*, *_received, or *_published under attribution=publish).

supported.description: Whether this profile can ever carry a value for the key. When false the record value is always null.

reason.description: Present when supported is false: platform (the network has no such metric), plan (insights not included or switched off), permission (the insights permission was not granted).

source.description: native - stored as the platform reports it. derived - computed by Postproxy.

platform_metric.description: The platform metric the key is read from (native keys only).

window.description: For unique-viewer keys, the window the value covers, ending on the record's day.

additive.description: true when values can be summed across days; false for unique-viewer keys.

missing_day.description: What a day missing from records, or a null value, means on or after coverage_start.

coverage_start.description: First day Postproxy holds a value for this key on this profile; null when supported but nothing has been stored yet.

provisional_from.description: First day whose values may still be revised on a later pull (Meta ~48h, YouTube ~72h, *_received trailing 2 days). null when values are final as soon as they appear.

get.description: Instagram only. Returns whether a user follows the profile's Instagram account (and vice versa), plus their verified badge and follower count, fetched live from Instagram's messaging user lookup. The user_id is the Instagram-scoped user id from a DM chat (participant_external_id) or a comment (author_external_id); Instagram only resolves users who have messaged or commented on your account. Lookups are cached for one second per user; the X-Cached response header says whether the payload came from cache.

parameters.description: Instagram-scoped user id (DM sender id or comment author id)

get.description: LinkedIn only. Turns a LinkedIn company page URL (or its slug) into the URN LinkedIn needs to render an @-mention — mentions are written into post text as @[Display Name](urn), e.g. @[Postproxy](urn:li:organization:110810308). Company, showcase and school pages all resolve; the page does not have to be one this connection administers. bearerAuth.description: API key sent as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. Keys are either full-access (entire account) or scoped to a single profile group. Create keys at https://app.postproxy.dev under Settings → API Keys.

ProfileGroupId.name: profile_group_id
ProfileGroupId.description: Profile group context for the request. Optional when the API key is scoped to a profile group (that group is used automatically); with a full-access key, defaults to the first profile group in the account.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional idempotency key (up to 255 characters; a UUID is ideal). Retrying a successful write with the same key replays the original response (with an Idempotent-Replay: true header) instead of executing again. Stored responses are kept for 24 hours; only 2xx responses are stored.

Unauthorized.description: Invalid, missing, or insufficient API key permissions.

NotFound.description: Resource does not exist or is not accessible.

Conflict.description: Duplicate submission, or a request with the same Idempotency-Key is still in flight.

MethodNotAllowed.description: Unsupported method for this platform or resource.

PlatformErrorDetails.description: Structured platform error (omitted when no platform error info is available).

platform_error_code.description: Error code returned by the platform API

platform_error_subcode.description: Error subcode returned by the platform API

platform_error_message.description: Error message returned by the platform API

postproxy_note.description: Additional context from Postproxy about the error

CommentAttachment.description: Media attached to a comment. Postproxy downloads each asset to durable storage; the url is stable once status is processed.

url.description: Stable storage URL to the asset. While status is pending, this temporarily falls back to the source URL on the platform until the file is mirrored to Postproxy storage.

status.description: pending (still being mirrored), processed (stored and ready), failed (could not be downloaded)

external_id.description: Platform-side identifier for the attachment (e.g. Facebook attachment target ID). Omitted when the platform did not provide one.

CommentMetadata.description: Additional author signals fetched asynchronously from the platform after the comment is ingested. Null until the lookup completes; individual keys may be absent depending on platform support.

author_fetched_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last author-info refresh

is_business_follow_user.description: The business profile follows the author (instagram)

Comment.description: A comment on a published post.

external_id.description: Platform's native comment ID (null for pending comments)

status.description: Comment status. Only published and failed are terminal — treat every other value as still in progress.

error.description: Error summary if the comment failed to publish (null otherwise)

author_avatar_url.description: Stable Postproxy storage URL of the author's profile picture once mirrored; the platform URL until then

parent_external_id.description: Parent comment's external ID (null for top-level comments)

like_count.description: Number of likes on the comment

permalink.description: Direct URL to the comment on the platform (when available)

attachments.description: Media attached to the comment. Empty array when there are none. Always empty on a freshly created (pending) comment.

external_edited_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last edit made through Postproxy (null if never edited)

posted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the comment was posted on the platform

replies.description: All replies (regardless of nesting depth) flattened under the root top-level comment, sorted by created_at ascending. Present on per-post list and get responses.

CommentListResponse.description: Paginated list of top-level comments for a post.

data.description: Array of top-level comment objects, each with a replies array

CommentCrossPostListResponse.description: Flat, paginated list of comments across posts and profiles. Replies are not nested: every comment is its own entry, linked to its parent by parent_external_id.

total.description: Total number of matching comments, replies included

post_id.description: ID of the post the comment belongs to

profile_id.description: ID of the profile the comment was left on

CommentCreateRequest.description: Payload for creating a comment or reply on a published post.

body.description: Comment text content. (The legacy text parameter is still accepted as an alias.)

parent_id.description: ID of comment to reply to (Postproxy ID or external ID). Omit to comment on the post itself.

ProfileComment.description: A profile-scoped comment — a Google Business Profile review, a Facebook Page recommendation, or a reply to one.

external_id.description: Platform's native resource ID (null while a reply is pending publication)

parent_external_id.description: External ID of parent review (null for top-level reviews)

body.description: Comment/review text. Google Business reviews can be star-only: body is null while platform_data.star_rating is still populated.

error.description: Error summary if an outgoing reply failed (null otherwise)

author_username.description: Display name of reviewer (null for your own replies)

platform_data.description: Platform-specific metadata (e.g. star_rating, update_time for Google reviews; recommendation_type for Facebook recommendations)

permalink.description: URL to the comment on the platform (the location's reviews page on Google or the Page's reviews tab on Facebook — shared by all reviews and replies on that location / Page; null if unavailable)

replies.description: Nested replies to this comment, sorted by created_at ascending (present on list/get responses)

ProfileCommentListResponse.description: Paginated list of top-level profile comments.

data.description: Array of top-level comment objects, each with a replies array

ProfileCommentCreateRequest.description: Payload for replying to an existing review. Top-level comments cannot be authored — parent_id is required.

parent_id.description: Postproxy ID or external ID of the review being replied to

body.description: Reply body. (The legacy text parameter is still accepted as an alias.)

DmChatMetadata.description: Platform-specific information about the participant, fetched asynchronously when the chat is first created and refreshed at most once per hour on inbound messages. Keys are only present when the platform returns a value — treat missing keys as unknown, not false.

page_id.description: Facebook — Page ID this chat is owned by (required for sending)

participant_fetched_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last recipient-info refresh

language_code.description: Telegram — IETF language tag reported by Telegram for the user

muted.description: Bluesky — whether the conversation is muted/archived

is_verified_user.description: Instagram — participant has a verified account

is_user_follow_business.description: Instagram — participant follows the business profile

is_business_follow_user.description: Instagram — the business profile follows the participant

referral.description: Latest ig.me / m.me link referral (latest referral wins)

last_referral_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the latest referral (opens the 24-hour messaging window)

DmChat.description: A 1:1 conversation between a profile and a participant.

profile_id.description: Profile hashid this chat belongs to

participant_avatar_url.description: Stable storage URL of the participant's profile picture (null until fetched)

last_inbound_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of last inbound message

last_outbound_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of last outbound message

last_message_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of last message in either direction

archived.description: Bluesky only — whether the chat is muted/archived

external_placement_id.description: The placement the chat runs on — the phone number id on WhatsApp, the Page id on Facebook chats that have one. Null otherwise.

group.description: True when the chat is a WhatsApp group rather than a 1:1 conversation.

within_messaging_window.description: WhatsApp only. Whether a free-form send is currently allowed — true for 24 hours after the customer’s last inbound message or referral. Outside it, send an approved template.

DmChatListResponse.description: Paginated list of chats for a profile.

DmChatCreateRequest.description: Payload for idempotently creating (or finding) a chat by participant.

participant_external_id.description: Platform participant ID (Instagram-scoped user ID for IG, PSID for Facebook, DID for Bluesky, the phone number for WhatsApp — any format, reduced to digits)

placement_id.description: Required on WhatsApp — the phone number id the conversation runs on. Optional on Facebook, where it records the Page an API-created chat sends from.

DmMessageAttachment.description: Media attached to a message. Inbound media is mirrored from the platform CDN to durable storage; outbound files are uploaded before the send. The url is stable and does not expire.

url.description: Stable storage URL. While status is pending this may temporarily fall back to the source URL.

external_id.description: Platform-side identifier (e.g. a Messenger sticker ID), when provided

DmReaction.description: A reaction on a message. Reflects the live state.

DmTappedAction.description: Set on inbound messages created by a tap of a quick reply, button postback, ice breaker, or Telegram inline-keyboard button. A tap also opens the 24-hour messaging window.

kind.description: quick_reply, postback (Meta buttons and ice breakers), or callback_query (Telegram inline keyboards)

DmQuickReply.description: A tappable chip shown above the participant's composer (Facebook and Instagram only). Chips disappear once one is tapped.

content_type.description: Optional; only "text" is accepted — Messenger's user_phone_number / user_email chips are not supported

DmButton.description: A button attached to the message itself (Facebook and Instagram only). Buttons stay in the thread.

payload.description: Required for postback buttons, 1000 characters or fewer

url.description: Required for web_url buttons, must be an https:// URL

DmCard.description: Extra fields for the card carrying buttons — renders a richer, product-style card. Requires buttons.

default_action.description: Action when the card itself is tapped

DmMessage.description: A direct message (inbound or outbound) in a chat.

external_comment_id.description: Set when the message was sent as a private reply to a comment

error_message.description: Last error from the platform (when failed)

platform_data.description: Raw platform webhook payload, passed through unchanged. Shape is platform- and event-specific and may change without notice — prefer the typed fields where available.

story_reply.description: Instagram only. Set on inbound messages that reply to one of your stories. The url is a short-lived Meta link tied to the story's lifetime (typically 24h or less) — not mirrored to Postproxy storage.

external_delivered_at.description: When the platform confirmed delivery (outbound; FB & IG only)

external_read_at.description: When the recipient read the message (outbound; FB & IG only)

external_edited_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent edit; body reflects the latest edit

reply_to_external_id.description: Platform message ID this message replies to (inbound replies, outbound reply_to_external_id, or a Telegram callback query's source)

reply_markup.description: Telegram only — the reply_markup attached to the message

quick_replies.description: Facebook and Instagram only — the chips sent with the message

buttons.description: Facebook and Instagram only — the buttons attached to the message

card.description: Facebook and Instagram only — the card fields (subtitle, image_url, default_action) sent alongside buttons

external_deleted_at.description: When the message was deleted/unsent on the platform (treat as redacted)

reactions.description: Reactions on the message. Reflects the live state.

is_unsupported.description: true when the platform marked the message as unsupported (e.g. an unprocessable voice clip)

template.description: WhatsApp only. The template a message was sent with — id, external_id, name, language, variables.

interactive.description: WhatsApp only. Outbound: the interactive object sent. Inbound: the customer’s reply to one — type "button_reply" / "list_reply" / "nfm_reply" with the id and title you assigned.

location.description: WhatsApp only. latitude, longitude, name, address — sent or received.

source.description: "synced" on an outbound WhatsApp message the team sent from the phone on a coexistence number.

DmMessageListResponse.description: Paginated list of messages in a chat.

DmMessageSendRequest.description: Payload for sending an outbound message. Each send accepts either text (body) or a single attachment (media), never both. On WhatsApp exactly one payload per send: one of body, media, template, interactive, location or contacts.

body.description: Message text. Required when media is empty. Capped at 220 characters when buttons are present.

media.description: A single media attachment. Accepts the same shapes as the Posts API — a multipart upload, a public URL, a base64 data URI, or a base64 hash. Currently one attachment per send (Meta Send API limit); passing more returns 422. Not supported on Bluesky (422).

items.description: A media attachment in any of the shapes accepted by the Posts API (public URL, base64 data URI, base64 hash, or multipart upload reference).

tag.description: Message tag for sending outside the 24-hour window. Facebook and Instagram only — ignored on Telegram. Extends the reply window to 7 days from the participant's last inbound message; for a human resolving the participant's own inquiry only, never promotional content. Rejected on WhatsApp, which has no HUMAN_AGENT tag — use a template or category "utility" instead.

reply_to_external_id.description: Telegram and WhatsApp. Platform message ID to thread the reply under — on WhatsApp the wamid, which renders the send as a quoted reply.

reply_markup.description: Telegram only. Inline keyboard (inline_keyboard), custom reply keyboard (keyboard, with one_time_keyboard / resize_keyboard), force_reply, or remove-keyboard payload — passed through to Telegram unchanged.

quick_replies.description: Facebook and Instagram only. Up to 13 tappable chips shown above the participant's composer. On Instagram, delivered only on a plain-text message (not combinable with media or buttons).

buttons.description: Facebook and Instagram only. Up to 3 buttons attached to the message. Requires body (capped at 220 characters); cannot be combined with media.

interactive.description: WhatsApp only. Meta’s interactive object unchanged — reply buttons (type "button"), lists ("list"), call-to-action URLs ("cta_url"), catalog products ("product" / "product_list") or Flows ("flow"). Session message: needs an open messaging window and cannot be sent to a group.

contacts.description: WhatsApp only. Array of Meta contact objects (name, phones, emails, …).

category.description: WhatsApp only. "utility" sends a plain text outside the 24-hour window via Meta’s Direct Send, where the account is eligible. Valid only alongside body; with any other payload returns 422.

link_preview.description: WhatsApp only. Render a preview for a link in body.

voice_note.description: WhatsApp only. Send an audio attachment as a voice note.

filename.description: WhatsApp only. Filename shown for a document attachment.

DmMessageEditRequest.description: Payload for editing an outbound Telegram message. At least one of body / reply_markup is required.

body.description: New text. For media messages this becomes the new caption.

reply_markup.description: New inline keyboard (or other reply_markup). Pass an empty {} to remove the existing keyboard.

DmMessageReactRequest.description: Payload for reacting to a message. Instagram's outbound reactions API accepts only love (you may pass an emoji alongside). Facebook Messenger expects a unicode emoji — Postproxy translates the named reactions before calling Meta; a supplied emoji always takes precedence over the named reaction for Messenger.

emoji.description: Unicode emoji. Forwarded to Instagram; on Messenger it overrides reaction as the literal value sent to Meta.

DmPrivateReplyRequest.description: Payload for sending a private reply DM to a comment's author.

DmIceBreaker.description: A predefined question Instagram shows a user opening a new thread with your business.

DmIceBreakersSetRequest.description: Payload for setting the profile's ice breakers. Setting ice breakers replaces the previous set.

ice_breakers.description: 1-4 items, each requiring question and payload

source.description: Origin of the post: postproxy (created via app or API) or imported (imported from a connected platform)

draft.description: Whether the post is a draft

scheduled_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp if scheduled, null otherwise

queue_id.description: Queue ID if the post belongs to a queue

queue_priority.description: Priority level if in a queue

platforms.description: Array of platform-specific posting results. For thread posts, this only describes the parent — each thread item carries its own platforms array.

thread.description: Array of thread child posts (only present for thread posts). Each item carries its own platforms array.

profile_name.description: Display name of the connected profile

status.description: Platform posting status: processing, published, failed, pending_deletion, deleted

params.description: Platform-specific parameters used for this post

error_details.description: Structured error details from the platform (null when no platform error info is available)

permalink.description: Direct URL to the published post on the platform. Null if not published or permalink is unavailable

on.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when insights were captured

platform_error_code.description: Error code returned by the platform API

platform_error_subcode.description: Error subcode returned by the platform API

platform_error_message.description: Error message returned by the platform API

postproxy_note.description: Additional context from Postproxy about the error

PostMedia.description: A media attachment on a post.

source_url.description: Original source URL if media was provided as a URL

url.description: Hosted URL of the processed file (null if not yet processed)

platforms.description: Per-platform formatting/upload errors for this attachment. Only included when at least one platform had an error processing this specific media file; omitted when there are no platform-level errors

PostMediaPlatformError.description: A platform-specific error for a media attachment (e.g. format/aspect ratio rejected on Instagram, file size too large on Twitter).

error.description: Error summary for this attachment on this platform

error_details.description: Structured platform error (omitted when no platform error info is available)

PostThreadChild.description: A thread child post. Carries its own platforms array with the same shape as the parent's, so a half-delivered thread is visible without extra requests.

id.description: Unique identifier (id) of the child post

body.description: Text content of the child post

platforms.description: Per-platform delivery results for this thread item (status, permalink, error, error_details)

PostCreateRequest.description: Request body for creating a post. Some platforms require media (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube); some platforms require text content.

scheduled_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp to schedule the post. Do not pass together with queue_id — the queue determines the scheduled time automatically

draft.description: If true, creates a draft that won't publish until reviewed

profiles.description: Array of profile IDs or platform names (e.g. "twitter", "instagram" — uses the first connected profile for that platform). All resolved profiles must belong to the same profile group.

media.description: Array of media URLs, base64 data URIs, or file uploads (multipart)

platforms.description: Platform-specific parameters, keyed by platform name (e.g. instagram, youtube). See Platform Parameters docs for all available options.

thread.description: Array of thread child posts. Threads are only supported on X (Twitter) and Threads; other platforms return a 422.

profile_group_id.description: ID of the profile group to resolve profiles against. If omitted, platform names resolve in the default group (first one on the account) and profile IDs are looked up across all groups your API key / user can access

queue_id.description: Queue ID — adds the post to a queue. The queue must belong to the same profile group as the resolved profiles

PostUpdateRequest.description: Request body for updating a post. All parameters are optional — only send the fields you want to change. profiles, media, and thread are full replaces; post fields and platforms are merged.

post.description: Merged with existing values — only the fields you include are changed

profiles.description: Full replace: all existing profile assignments are removed and replaced with the new set (array of profile IDs or platform names)

platforms.description: Merged with existing platform params. When sent together with profiles, platform params are applied to the new profile set (same as create)

media.description: Full replace: all existing media attachments are destroyed and replaced. Send an empty array to remove all media

thread.description: Full replace: all existing thread children are destroyed and rebuilt from the new array. Send an empty array to remove all thread children. Thread children automatically inherit the parent's profiles, scheduling, and draft status

queue_id.description: Assign the post to a queue

profile_group_id.description: Scope the lookup to a specific profile group

PostThreadItemRequest.description: A thread child post. Position is determined by array order (first item = first reply).

body.description: Text content for this thread post

media.description: Array of media URLs (same format as top-level media)

PostStatsResponse.description: Stats snapshots keyed by post id. For thread posts, stats from all posts in the thread (parent + children) are included under the parent post's ID.

platforms.description: Array of platform objects for this post

stats.description: Normalized metrics — the same key means the same thing across platforms (available keys vary by platform)

raw_stats.description: The same metrics as a flat key-value object under their original platform names (e.g. like_count for Twitter, impressionCount for LinkedIn). Null for snapshots recorded before July 20, 2026

recorded_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the snapshot was captured

Queue.description: A posting queue that automatically schedules posts into recurring weekly timeslots, with priority-based ordering.

enabled.description: Whether the queue is active. When paused (false), posts in the queue will not be published even if their scheduled time arrives

jitter.description: Random offset in minutes (+/-) applied to scheduled times (0-60, default: 0)

QueueTimeslot.description: A weekly timeslot: a day of the week plus a time, interpreted in the queue's timezone.

QueueTimeslotInput.description: Timeslot attributes for create/update. To add, pass day and time; to remove, pass id and _destroy: true.

_destroy.description: Pass true together with id to remove the timeslot

QueueCreateRequest.description: Request body for creating a queue.

profile_group_id.description: Profile group ID to connect the queue to

QueueUpdateRequest.description: Request body for updating a queue. Any changes to timezone or timeslots trigger a rearrangement of all queued posts.

queue_timeslots_attributes.description: Add timeslots (day + time) or remove them (id + _destroy: true)

CalendarEvent.description: A social media calendar event for 2026.

category.description: post_trigger: good opportunity to post; sensitive: post with care; no_post: brands should stay silent or share only respectful acknowledgment

countries.description: Country codes (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) where applicable, or null for global events

name.description: Display name of the connected account.

username.description: Handle on the platform (without @). null when the platform does not expose one.

platform_id.description: The account's ID on the platform.

status.description: Platform connection status. inactive might mean disconnected or suspended on a platform.

profile_group_id.description: ID of the profile group this belongs to.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the connection expires (if applicable). null when the token does not expire or has a refresh token.

post_count.description: Number of posts made through this profile.

avatar_url.description: Stable Postproxy storage URL of the account's profile picture, resized to 256x256. null until it has been mirrored. For facebook this is the connecting user's picture; each Page's picture is avatar_url on its placement.

platform_url.description: Public URL of the account on the platform. null when the platform has no stable public profile URL (e.g. linkedin, google_business).

placements_sync_status.description: State of the latest pull of this profile's placements. The pull runs in the background right after connecting and can take several minutes on profiles with many pages/locations. null for platforms without placements and for telegram, whose channels arrive via webhook.

ProfilePlacement.description: A placement a profile can publish to (Facebook Page, LinkedIn organization or personal profile, Pinterest board, Telegram channel, Google Business location).

id.description: Platform-specific placement ID. null for personal profile (LinkedIn).

avatar_url.description: Stable Postproxy storage URL of the placement's picture, resized to 256x256 (Facebook Pages). null until it has been mirrored and for networks without one.

metadata.description: Extra per-placement data Postproxy stores. For Google Business this carries the location's place_id (Google Maps Place ID). {} when there's nothing extra.

Placement.description: Account-wide placement record (Facebook Page, LinkedIn organization, Pinterest board, Telegram channel, Google Business location). One record exists per account, platform, and platform ID, even when several connected profiles can see it; exactly one linked profile is the active profile that posting and webhooks route through.

id.description: Placement ID. Postproxy's own ID, used in placement URLs — not the platform ID.

external_id.description: Platform-specific ID — the value used as page_id / chat_id when creating posts, and returned as id by the per-profile List placements endpoint.

avatar_url.description: Stable Postproxy storage URL of the placement's picture, resized to 256x256 (Facebook Pages). null until it has been mirrored and for networks without one.

status.description: active (the active profile is connected), orphaned (the active profile is disconnected — posting is paused until you switch to a connected profile), or removed (access was revoked on the platform).

linked_profiles.description: Every profile that can see this placement — the candidates for Set active profile.

PlacementProfileRef.description: Compact profile reference on a placement.

connected.description: Whether the profile is currently connected.

ProfilePostSync.description: A post sync run: the sync fired when the profile connects, the recurring poll, or a backfill. Runs are kept for 30 days.

started_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the run began.

completed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when it finished or failed.

posts_seen.description: Posts the platform returned across the run.

posts_imported.description: Posts that were new and got created. Lower than posts_seen whenever the run re-read posts you already have.

backfill_from.description: The date floor requested. null for connect and scheduled runs.

oldest_posted_at.description: Publish date of the oldest post the run reached - how far back it has walked.

error.description: Platform error message when status is failed.

ProfileChatSync.description: A chat sync run: the pull fired when the profile connects (or direct messages are enabled) or a backfill you start. Runs are kept for 30 days.

started_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the run began.

completed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when it finished or failed.

chats_seen.description: Conversations the platform returned across the run.

messages_imported.description: Messages that were new and got created. Messages you already have are skipped and not counted.

backfill_from.description: The date floor requested. null for connect runs.

oldest_updated_at.description: Last-activity time of the oldest conversation the run reached - how far back it has walked.

error.description: Platform error message when status is failed.

ProfileGroup.description: An organizational container that groups related social media profiles together.

name.description: Display name of the profile group.

profiles_count.description: Number of connected profiles in this group.

WebhookSubscription.description: A webhook subscription that receives event deliveries at an HTTPS URL.

url.description: HTTPS URL that receives webhook events.

events.description: Subscribed event types (["*"] means all events).

secret.description: Signing secret used to verify webhook signatures. Only included when fetching a single webhook or immediately after creation.

WebhookDelivery.description: A delivery attempt of a webhook event.

event_id.description: Event delivery ID, prefixed with whevt_.

response_status.description: HTTP status code returned by the endpoint.

attempt_number.description: Attempt number (deliveries are retried up to 5 times with exponential backoff).

WebhookEventEnvelope.description: Envelope shared by every webhook delivery.

id.description: Delivery ID, prefixed with whevt_. Matches the X-Postproxy-Delivery header.

type.description: Event type (e.g. platform_post.published). Matches the X-Postproxy-Event header.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the event was generated.

object.description: The event-specific resource - shape varies per event type.
Imported post payload - a post published outside Postproxy and discovered during a profile sync.

posted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the post was originally published on the platform.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the post was imported into Postproxy.

profile.description: Profile the post was imported from.

public_id.description: Platform's public-facing post ID/shortcode (used in permalinks).

object.description: Platform Post payload shape. The status and error fields reflect the outcome.

platform_id.description: External post ID on the platform (null until published).

insights.description: Normalized key-value stats from the platform (varies by network).

raw_stats.description: The same metrics under their original platform key names. null for snapshots recorded before July 20, 2026.

object.description: Profile stats snapshot. Snapshots are captured roughly every 23 hours per profile; for networks with placements the event fires once per placement on each polling cycle.

placement_id.description: Platform-specific placement ID. null for networks without placements.

stats.description: Platform-specific metrics. Shape varies by network.

recorded_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the snapshot was captured.

profile_id.description: ID of the profile that owns the post.

parent_external_id.description: Parent comment ID (null for top-level comments).

author_avatar_url.description: Stable Postproxy storage URL of the author's profile picture once mirrored; the platform URL until then

external_edited_at.description: ISO 8601 time of the last edit confirmed through Postproxy (null if never edited)

posted_at.description: ISO 8601 time when posted on the platform.

object.description: Profile comment payload shape - a profile-scoped comment such as a Google Business review, a Facebook Page recommendation, or a published reply.

parent_external_id.description: Parent review external ID (null for top-level reviews).

author_username.description: Reviewer display name (null for your own replies).

posted_at.description: ISO 8601 time when posted on the platform.

object.description: The full direct message object, reflecting state after the event. See the Direct Messages reference for the message object fields.

message.description: The full message object, reflecting the post-reaction state (the reactions array already has the reactor added for react, or removed for unreact).

sender_external_id.description: Platform ID of whoever placed/removed the reaction (participant PSID/IGSID, or your own profile.external_id for business reactions).

emoji.description: Unicode emoji; may be absent on Messenger and on unreact events.

object.description: Referral payload - a participant entered a DM thread via an ig.me / m.me link carrying a ref parameter. Facebook & Instagram only.

chat.description: The full chat object, with the referral already stored under metadata.referral.

ref.description: The ref parameter from the link.

source.description: Where the referral came from (e.g. SHORTLINK).

id.description: API key ID, used in the revoke URL.

profile_group_id.description: The profile group the key is scoped to.

token.description: The secret bearer token. Returned only in the create response.

WhatsAppTemplateSend.description: WhatsApp only. Sends an approved message template instead of body. Works inside or outside the 24-hour window and re-opens it.

id.description: Template hashid or Meta id. Either id or name is required.

name.description: Template name. Add language when the name exists in several languages, otherwise 409.

variables.description: Values as strings, in order: header text variables, then body variables, then one value per dynamic URL button. For POSITIONAL templates the count must equal the template’s variable_count.

button_params.description: Overrides for buttons needing runtime parameters — each { index, sub_type, parameters } in Meta’s shape. sub_type is url, copy_code, flow, quick_reply or voice_call.

header_media.description: { "link": "https://…" } or { "id": "<meta media id>" } for templates with an IMAGE, VIDEO or DOCUMENT header.

WhatsAppTemplate.description: A WhatsApp message template on the connected WhatsApp Business Account.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. With language it identifies the template on Meta.

language.description: Meta language code, e.g. en_US, pt_BR, de

status.description: Meta review status. Only APPROVED templates can be sent.

components.description: Meta’s component array — HEADER, BODY, FOOTER, BUTTONS.

message_send_ttl_seconds.description: Time-to-live for undelivered sends, when the template overrides Meta’s default.

rejected_reason.description: Present when Meta rejected the template.

quality_score.description: Meta’s quality score once scored, e.g. { "score": "GREEN" }.

variable_count.description: How many variables a send of this template expects.

WhatsAppTemplateListResponse.description: Every matching template, ordered by name then language. Not paginated.

WhatsAppTemplateCreateRequest.description: Creates a custom template from components, or copies one of Meta’s pre-approved library templates.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. Unique per language on the account.

components.description: Required for a custom template. Meta’s component array; a component with variables needs an example for review.

message_send_ttl_seconds.description: AUTHENTICATION 30–900, UTILITY 30–43200, MARKETING 43200–2592000. -1 keeps Meta’s default on AUTHENTICATION or UTILITY.

library_template_name.description: Required to copy a Meta library template; components is then not needed. A library copy is approved immediately.

WhatsAppTemplateUpdateRequest.description: At least one field is required. Editing components sends the template back to Meta review.

components.description: Replaces the whole component array. Status returns to PENDING until Meta approves it again.

message_send_ttl_seconds.description: New TTL within the category’s range. -1 is not accepted on update.

scope.description: Deleting by name with no language removes every language variant.

template.description: Meta’s library entry — body, expected inputs and buttons. Null when the name is unknown.

phone.description: Live number state from Meta: display_phone_number, verified_name, name_status, new_name_status, quality_rating, messaging_limit_tier, throughput, status, platform_type, is_official_business_account.

waba.description: Account state: name, account_review_status, business_verification_status, timezone_id, ownership_type. Null when the account-level read fails.

business_profile.description: about, address, description, email, websites, vertical, profile_picture_url. Meta omits fields that were never set.

WhatsAppBusinessProfileUpdateRequest.description: Send only what changes; at least one field besides phone_number_id is required.

vertical.description: Meta industry value, e.g. RETAIL, RESTAURANT, PROF_SERVICES, OTHER.

display_name.description: name, status, new_name_status (null when no change is pending), phone_number.

status.description: Meta’s status lowercased — e.g. approved, reserved, pending, or none when the number has no username.

users.description: Phone numbers in any format, or wa_ids.

WhatsAppBlockUsersResponse.description: Returns 200 even when some numbers could not be blocked; those are listed in failed with Meta’s reasons.

WhatsAppConversionEventRequest.description: Reports an outcome back to Meta for Click-to-WhatsApp ad optimization. Requires a chat whose ctwa_clid was captured, and a Conversions API dataset on the account.

event_id.description: Your unique id for the event; Meta dedupes on it.

chat_id.description: The chat the customer arrived in. One of chat_id or phone is required.

phone.description: The customer’s phone number instead; the most recently active chat with it is used.

event_time.description: Unix seconds or ISO 8601. Defaults to now.

email.description: SHA-256 hashed before it leaves Postproxy.

external_id.description: Your customer id. SHA-256 hashed before it leaves Postproxy.

test_code.description: Meta test event code, to see the event in Events Manager without affecting optimization.

dataset_id.description: Send to a specific dataset instead of the account’s own.
